title: Runtime Health Contracts and Self-Heal Orchestration
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Overview:

This page defines a set of Runtime Health Contracts (RHCs) and an associated self-heal orchestration blueprint for platform services that run Redwood's inference runtime. The RHCs make implicit operational expectations explicit (latency envelope, token-throughput, cache hit floor, KV store latency) and prescribe automated remediation actions and safe operator handoff points.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to mitigation for common degradations (cold-start tail, KV-thrash, GPU interference)
- Make automated remediation auditable and reversible
- Provide a testable contract for teams to validate service changes in canaries and load labs

Scope:
- Applies to core runtime services (request-router, batch-scheduler, prefix-cache, kv-store-proxy, model-proxy).
- Excludes customer-managed on-prem connectors and external partner gateways (those have separate contracts).

Key definitions:
- Runtime Health Contract (RHC): a declarative set of SLI thresholds, remediation steps (automated/manual), and safety guards for a service or component.
- Self-Heal Orchestrator (SHO): the platform controller that evaluates RHCs, triggers remediation playbooks, and records actions to the audit log.
- Operator Handoff Threshold: the earliest SLO breach severity where SHO must create a P2 and notify oncall.

RHC example (summary table):
| Component | Primary SLIs | Alert trigger | Auto-remediation | Operator handoff | Recovery target | Owner |
|-----------|--------------|---------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|-------|
| prefix-cache | 95p request latency, hit-rate | 10% hit-rate drop sustained >5m OR 95p latency >250ms | eviction policy refresh -> async prefix prewarm -> reduce expiry | P2 if >15m unresolved | restore hit-rate to within 5% baseline | eng-serving-runtime/cache |
| batch-scheduler | median dispatch latency, queue depth | queue depth > pre-configured burst threshold for 2m | scale up pool, backpressure non-urgent tenants | P1 if failure to scale | queue depth back to target | eng-platform/scheduler |

Self-Heal orchestration patterns:
1) Observe: SHO subscribes to tokenized SLIs and annotation streams.
2) Correlate: SHO uses signal fingerprinting (prefix affected, model id, region) to pick candidate remediation playbooks.
3) Validate: run quick hypothesis check (smoke trace against a shadow replica).
4) Execute: run the selected auto-remediation path (predefined safe actions).
5) Monitor & Escalate: if metrics do not return to recovery target within the specified window, escalate to operator handoff.

Safe actions (order of preference):
- Non-disruptive config nudges: reduce non-critical batching window, tighten tenant soft-limits.
- Read-only repairs: clear a stale cache shard, resend failing prefix cache prewarm requests.
- Capacity adjustments: spin temporary burst workers in same AZ, toggle GPU binding relaxations.
- Fallback routing: transparently route a % of traffic to a cheaper, compatible model variant with lower latency requirement.
- Graceful drain and restart: last-resort restart of misbehaving replica with pre-warmed rehydration sequence.

Runbook: Auto-remediation flow (operator-facing steps):
1) SHO detects SLI breach and starts remediation ID <auto-xxxxx>.
2) System performs Hypothesis Check (10–30s). If hypothesis fails, SHO logs and attempts alternative playbook.
3) SHO performs Action A (e.g., scale up 2x) with a 90s stabilization window.
4) If metrics meet recovery target, close the incident with remediation notes and metric snapshot.
5) If not, SHO attempts Action B (e.g., cache shard rebind). After second failure or 15m elapsed, SHO opens a P2, posts runbook link to #oncall-runtime and calls the operator according to page routing.

Operator checklist on P2 handoff:
- Confirm incident scope: affected prefixes, models, tenants, regions.
- Validate SHO actions and roll forward/rollback as needed.
- Collect: heap profiles, kernel scheduler traces, GPU utilization, KV latency traces.
- Execute manual remediation (if applicable): forced failover to warm pool, manual prefix rehydration, model-swap to compatible variant.
- Postmortem: tag incident with RHC id, include replay dataset used for SLO regression tests.

Observability and dashboards:
- Recommended dashboard panels: SLI heatmap (component x region), action timeline (SHO actions + result), tenant impact map, prereq signals (GPU temp/PCIe errors, KV latency percentiles).
- Suggested alert cadence: SHO-first for low-severity breaches (auto attempt then jittered retry), direct pager for operator handoff thresholds.

Simulation and validation:
- Unit test suggestions: RHC unit tests validate action selection for synthetic fingerprints.
- Integration tests: run in canary lane using traffic replay top-10 tenants; SHO must succeed in automated remediation for 4/5 seeded degradations.
- Load lab: inject KV latency, GPU preemption events, and prefix cache storms; record SHO action success rate and false-positive rate.

Rollout plan and milestones:
1) Q1 2026 — Pilot RHCs for prefix-cache and batch-scheduler in eu-west-1 (operator-approved).
2) Q2 2026 — Expand to model-proxy and request-router; add runbook automation for tenant-aware fallbacks.
3) Q3 2026 — Default SHO enabled for all non-critical tenants; integrate with console audit timeline.

Appendix: example policy YAML snippet (example only):

policy_id: rhc-prefix-cache-v1
component: prefix-cache
slis:
  - name: hit_rate_5m
    target: 0.85
    window: 5m
triggers:
  - condition: hit_rate_5m < 0.75 for 5m
    actions: [prewarm-prefix, reduce-eviction-window, notify-sho]
safety_guards:
  - max_action_concurrency: 1
  - max_retries: 2
operator_handoff: 15m
owner: eng-serving-runtime/cache
